themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints surged to 67 THIS WEEK—a 426% spike from the 8-week baseline of 12.8 per week—coinciding with a separate 900% spike in street sweeping complaints (5 THIS WEEK vs 0.5 avg), signaling potential widespread pavement, pothole, or drainage failures across Morris Park/Pelham Parkway.
evidence: Street Condition complaints: 67 THIS WEEK vs 12.8-week average (z-score: 8.5, severity: high)
Street Sweeping complaints: 5 THIS WEEK vs 0.5-week average (z-score: 9.0, severity: highest)
Root/Sewer/Sidewalk Condition complaints: 6 THIS WEEK vs 0.9-week average (z-score: 4.87), suggesting subsurface infrastructure breakdown
reporting_angles: Map the worst streets: interview DOT about which corridors are seeing emergency repairs this week
Subsurface story: are aging sewers and roots causing pavement collapse? Cross-reference sewer complaints (up 348% last week) with street failures

themes_detail.label: Homeless Services Surge
themes_detail.summary: Homeless person assistance complaints skyrocketed 1500% LAST WEEK (4 complaints vs 0.2-week average, z-score: 8.66), the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset, indicating either a concentrated encampment emergency, policy change, or acute service gap in the district.
evidence: Homeless Person Assistance complaints: 4 LAST WEEK vs 0.2-week average (z-score: 8.66, severity: highest spike in dataset)
No concurrent Reddit discussions or local news mentions suggest under-reported crisis
Community board budget requests prioritize 'park safety through more security staff,' suggesting baseline concern about street conditions
reporting_angles: Ground truth: where exactly are these complaints concentrated? Visit parks and transit hubs flagged in 311 data
Service capacity: are NYPD Homeless Outreach teams and DHS shelter placement overwhelmed right now?

themes_detail.label: Sewer & Drainage Emergency
themes_detail.summary: Sewer complaints jumped 348% LAST WEEK (14 vs 3.1-week average, z-score: 5.72), while Root/Sewer/Sidewalk complaints are up 586% THIS WEEK (6 vs 0.9 avg)—a dual signal suggesting acute sewer backups, root intrusion, or DEP infrastructure failure affecting multiple blocks.
evidence: Sewer complaints: 14 LAST WEEK vs 3.1-week average (z-score: 5.72, severity: high)
Root/Sewer/Sidewalk Condition complaints: 6 THIS WEEK vs 0.9-week average (z-score: 4.87, severity: high)
Community board has made 'clean catch basins' a repeated DEP capital budget request, indicating endemic drainage issues
reporting_angles: DEP response: what emergency repairs or flushing operations did DEP initiate in response to last week's spike?
Aging infrastructure: is this district on DEP's priority list for sewer main replacement?

themes_detail.label: Maintenance & Facility Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or Facility complaints spiked 850% TWO WEEKS AGO (19 complaints vs 2-week average of 2.0, z-score: 8.78), suggesting public facility neglect across parks, playgrounds, or municipal buildings—a signal that aligns with repeated CB budget requests for park reconstruction and security.
evidence: Maintenance or Facility complaints: 19 TWO WEEKS AGO vs 2.0-week average (z-score: 8.78, severity: high)
Community board repeatedly requests 'reconstruct or upgrade a park or amenity' and 'enhance park safety through more security staff'—suggests chronic neglect
284 DOB alteration permits filed in last 90 days may indicate ongoing private construction activity masking public facility decay
reporting_angles: Parks audit: which public facilities (playgrounds, rec centers, comfort stations) are generating maintenance complaints?
Resource gap: is Parks Department understaffed or under-budgeted for routine maintenance in this district?

themes_detail.label: Traffic Signal Outages
themes_detail.summary: Traffic Signal Condition complaints surged 384% LAST WEEK (23 complaints vs 4.8-week average, z-score: 6.1), creating potential traffic safety and congestion hazards across Morris Park/Pelham Parkway intersections.
evidence: Traffic Signal Condition complaints: 23 LAST WEEK vs 4.8-week average (z-score: 6.1, severity: high)
Concurrent spike in street condition complaints (426% THIS WEEK) may indicate DOT resource strain across multiple categories
No community board budget request specifically for traffic signals suggests this may be unexpected deterioration
reporting_angles: DOT emergency response: how many signals were out and for how long? Any collision increases correlated with outages?
Maintenance backlog: is DOT's signal repair team understaffed or dealing with broader electrical grid issues?
